title: Kailasa Mandir: ek hi pathar, upar se neeche kaata gaya
source: Indian Culture portal (Govt. of India) · Britannica · Live History India

captions.instagram:
Hey, want to hear something? A whole temple... without joining a single brick?

Ek poora mandir — EK HI CHATTAN se kaata gaya! 🛕 Ellora ka Kailasa Mandir upar se neeche ki taraf tarasha gaya, ~300 ft lamba aur ~175 ft chauda, 1,200 saal se bhi pehle!

Sources: Indian Culture portal (Govt. of India), Britannica, Live History India.
Photos: Arian Zwegers / Flickr (CC BY 2.0); Arian Zwegers / Flickr (CC BY 2.0).

claims.claim: The Kailasa temple (Ellora Cave 16, Maharashtra) is carved entirely out of a single rock
It was carved from the top of the rock downward
It is about 300 feet long and 175 feet wide
It was made in the Rashtrakuta period, generally attributed to King Krishna I (8th century) — over 1,200 years ago
The Ellora Caves are a UNESCO World Heritage Site (1983)

verify_note: Dating: Rashtrakuta, 8th century; said 'राष्ट्रकूट राजाओं के समय' (not one king).
